title: Night Shoot on Stage 9
occasion: the night shoot of a big-budget period film, three weeks behind schedule
blurb: Lights, haveli set, two hundred crew and a superstar who won't come out of his vanity van. The only scene nobody rehearsed was the murder.

archetypes.role: the ageing superstar playing the hero
archetypes.traits: vain, generous with juniors, terrified of being replaced
archetypes.voice: Grand, theatrical Hindi-English; sometimes talks about himself in the third person.

archetypes.role: the debutante heroine, a star kid
archetypes.traits: insecure, rebellious, always compared to her mother
archetypes.voice: South Bombay English: 'like', 'so basically'; switches to Hindi when upset.

archetypes.traits: brilliant, cruel on set, behind schedule
archetypes.voice: Intense, quick Hinglish: 'cut-cut', 'from the top'; swears mildly.

archetypes.role: the producer, who is over budget and in debt
a spot boy who has worked in films for twenty years
archetypes.traits: invisible, observant, loyal to the hero
gossipy, loyal, knows every scar and secret

archetypes.role: the choreographer, a former backup dancer
archetypes.voice: Energetic Hinglish; counts 'five-six-seven-eight' and calls everyone 'baby'.

archetypes.role: the screenwriter whose script has been rewritten five times
archetypes.voice: Dry, literary English with Urdu words.

archetypes.traits: ruthless, protective, always on two phones
archetypes.voice: Corporate English: 'basically', 'let me be very clear'.

archetypes.role: the first assistant director, who runs the set
archetypes.traits: exhausted, ambitious, sleeps two hours a night
archetypes.voice: Rushed Hinglish, like on a walkie: 'copy', 'lock it', 'roll sound'.

archetypes.traits: quiet, rough, the only one who follows safety rules

archetypes.traits: nosy, charming, digging for a scoop
